title: Reading a document without downloading it
summary: Spreadsheets, slide decks, reports and PDFs open inside the article. Here is what each one looks like, and why nothing ever leaves your browser.
author: Snoopy HQ Engineering
kicker: Four attachments, four formats, no downloads required.

sections.title: Why previews instead of downloads
paragraphs: A link to a spreadsheet asks a reader to leave the page, wait for a download, find the file and open an application that may not be installed. Most people simply do not bother, and the evidence behind a story goes unread.

Every attachment on this site opens where it sits. The file is parsed by your own browser, so nothing is uploaded to a service and nothing is sent anywhere. The original remains one click away for anyone who wants it, but reading it is no longer conditional on downloading it.
The four documents below exist to demonstrate each supported format. Their contents are invented for the purpose.

sections.title: A spreadsheet
paragraphs: Tabular data is the format that suffers most from being hidden behind a download. This inventory has eleven columns and a hundred and twenty rows, which is enough to show column resizing and scrolling behaviour without becoming a chore to read.

documents.title: Collection inventory
documents.caption: Eleven columns and 120 rows of demonstration data, for testing wide tables and scrolling.

sections.title: A slide deck
paragraphs: Presentations carry their own theme, fonts and layout rules. The viewer renders them inside an isolated document tree, so a deck's styling can never leak out and restyle the article around it.

documents.title: Collecting season 2026
documents.caption: A six-slide demonstration deck: title, bullets, a table, a pull quote and a two-column layout.

sections.title: A written report
paragraphs: Word documents keep their heading hierarchy, lists, tables and page breaks. This one runs to two pages so the flow across a page boundary is visible.

documents.title: Field notes: shelf photography
documents.caption: A two-page demonstration report with headings, lists, two tables and an explicit page break.

sections.title: A PDF
paragraphs: PDFs get a page navigator, zoom and fit controls. The renderer streams the file with range requests rather than downloading it whole, which is what keeps a long document responsive from the first page.

documents.title: Care and handling notes
documents.caption: A four-page demonstration PDF with tables and a pull quote, for page navigation and zoom.

sections.title: How it loads
paragraphs: None of the machinery above reaches you until you ask for it. The page itself ships only the attachment cards. Moving a cursor towards one quietly begins fetching the viewer, and the document itself is only read once the preview is opened.
A reader who never opens an attachment downloads none of it.
